newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dehaene says EMI chief "well placed" to head ECB.
newsitem.headline: Dehaene says EMI chief "well placed" to head ECB.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene says the head of the European Monetary Institute (EMI) would be well placed to become president of the European Central Bank (ECB) which is due to replace it in 1999.

"If the president of the EMI does his job well in the run-up to monetary union and enjoys the confidence of his colleagues, he would be in a very strong position when it is time to appoint the president of the bank," Dehaene told reporters in The Hague on Tuesday night.

Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg is due to take over as head of the EMI in July of this year and had been widely expected to become first president of the ECB which will launch the new European Union currency, the Euro, in January 1999.
French officials, including President Jacques Chirac, have said in recent months that Duisenberg will not automatically become the ECB's first president.
Some of them have alluded to a tacit agreement between France and Germany that a Frenchman should head the ECB in return for the decision to site the bank in Frankfurt.
